none: PAS FindID 1014577: Early Medieval coin: Merovingian Frankish tremissis
contea di ritrovamento: North Lincolnshire (Inghilterra e Galles)

Gold coin. Merovingian ‘national series’ tremissis of Metz mint, as kindly identified by the finder, pierced with a probably drilled hole of diameter 1.6mm at 3 O’clock obverse. Suggested date: Early Medieval, 587-670. Obverse description: Bust diademed and cuirassed right. Obverse inscription: METTIS CIVETATI *. Reverse description: plain cross in wreath; V C[reversed] in upper angles; plain initial cross. Reverse inscription: +ANSOALDVS M[O]NET, piercing through O. Diameter: 14.4mm, Weight: 1.23gms, die axis: 12. The piercing of the coin may be intended to convert it to an amulet with the cross displayed, perhaps as a miniature and ready-made version of the pendants…
